identity: XZ=-ZX with invertible involutions implies det(XZ)=det(-ZX)=(-1)^d det(XZ)
theorem: Two Hermitian involutions are invertible. If they anticommute in complex dimension d, determinants give det(XZ)=(-1)^d det(ZX)=(-1)^d det(XZ). For odd d this is impossible. Hence exact anticommuting involutive Clifford pairs exist only in even dimension; the even-dimensional nonuniqueness lift has no odd-dimensional analogue.
